title_en: Answers on the explanation of hadith 1
body_ar:
شرح العبارة: (كالريح المرسلة)

ما وجه الشبه في قول ابن عباس: "كالريح المرسلة؟"

أن الريح المرسلة سريعة جدا وتذرو كل ما تمر عليه وتقلبه، فكذلك عطاء رسول الله (ص) يأتي على كل شيء فلا يدع شيئا في بيته إلا أعطاه وكذلك في سرعة العطاء فيعطي قبل أن يسأل ويصل عطاؤه أبعد الجهات كالريح التي تقطع المسافات الشاسعة في الوقت القصير.

----------------------

شرح الحديث الذي ورد فيه: (..قوم حدثاء الأسنان)

ما معنى قول الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم (قوم حدثاء الأسنان) وأطلب منكم أن تتفضلوا بشرح الحديث كله؟

قول الرسول (ص) إن هؤلاء الخوارج قوم حدثاء الأسنان أي أنهم ليسوا من أصحاب رسول الله (ص) بل هم من النابتة التي نشأت بعد ذلك، وهذا من أمارات نبوته (ص)، فإنه حدث عنهم هذا الحديث وقد حصلت الفتنة في أزمان الصحابة فلم يدخلها أحد من أصحاب رسول الله (ص) وإنما دخلتها هذه النابتة التي هي حدثاء ..
body_en:
Explanation of the expression: "like the loosed wind".

What is the point of resemblance in Ibn ʿAbbas's words: "like the loosed wind"?

The loosed wind is exceedingly swift, and it scatters everything it passes over and overturns it. Just so, the giving of the Messenger of God, upon whom be peace, came upon everything: he would leave nothing in his house without giving it away. And likewise in the swiftness of the giving: he would give before he was asked, and his giving would reach the most distant quarters, like the wind that covers vast distances in a short time.

----------------------

Explanation of the hadith in which occurs: "..a people young in years".

What is the meaning of the Messenger's words, upon whom be God's blessing and peace, "a people young in years"? And I ask you to be so good as to explain the whole hadith.

The Messenger's words, upon whom be peace, that these Kharijites are "a people young in years" mean that they are not among the Companions of the Messenger of God, upon whom be peace; rather they are of the crop that sprang up after that. This is among the signs of his prophethood, upon whom be peace, for he gave this report concerning them; and the tribulation came about in the times of the Companions, and not one of the Companions of the Messenger of God, upon whom be peace, entered into it — rather it was entered into by this crop, who are young ..

flags.arabic: وأطلب منكم أن تتفضلوا بشرح الحديث كله؟
flags.context: the second limb of the second question — a request to explain the whole hadith, which the published text does not do
options: display with a prominent banner stating that only the phrase asked about is explained and that the text breaks off
withhold the second entry until the full text behind the .docx download is obtained
display the excerpt as it stands
flags.note: CRITICAL FOR DISPLAY. The questioner asks two things: the meaning of one phrase, and an explanation of the whole hadith. The published text explains the phrase and then breaks off mid-clause without touching the second request. The hadith in question is the one describing the Kharijites, which carries weight in contemporary debate, so a reader who takes the fragment for a complete treatment is materially misled. The full material is behind the .docx download in source_download_link.

flags.context: بل هم من النابتة التي نشأت بعد ذلك
flags.note: Al-nābitah is a vegetal metaphor for a generation that has newly come up, and in this usage it carries a dismissive edge. 'The upstarts' makes the edge explicit and 'the new growth' removes it; option 0 keeps the metaphor and lets the edge sit where the Arabic puts it. The word should be rendered consistently across the corpus once a choice is fixed.

flags.context: the phrase the question is about
options: young in age, literally 'new of tooth'
flags.note: Asnān is literally 'teeth' and by extension 'age'; ḥadīth here is 'new, recent'. The phrase is idiomatic for youth and the Sheikh glosses it as such. Since the question is expressly about the meaning of the phrase, a reviewer may prefer option 1 so that the English reader can see why the question was asked at all.

translator_notes: TYPING DECISION. The source presents this page as 'answers' (ajwibah) to questions put to the Sheikh, in the same question-and-answer form as the written fatwas. It is typed 'article' rather than 'fatwa' because it contains no ruling on an act: the glossary fixes fatwā as 'a considered legal opinion', and this page is explanatory. The site must not display it as a fatwa, or readers will take its contents for rulings.
Qur'anic and hadith renderings in this file are interpretive translations of meaning, offered to carry the Sheikh's argument in English. They are not a substitute for the Arabic.

In the source, the answer begins with the elliptical particle 'anna ('[the answer is] that ...'), the Joomla fatwa template's standing form. The English drops the particle and begins the sentence directly; no content is added or removed by this.
The date shown by the CMS is a bulk-upload timestamp shared by every item in this range, not the date the Sheikh gave the answer. The real date of composition is unknown. See date_is_cms_bulk_upload.

EXCERPT ONLY. The published text breaks off and the full material is offered as a .docx download ('taḥmīl al-māddah'). The English ends exactly where the Arabic ends. The download-link label has been removed from body_ar as a navigation element and recorded in source_download_link.
This page is a compilation of two separate answers, divided in the source by a row of hyphens, which has been kept in both body_ar and body_en as the structural marker it is.

'The loosed wind' renders al-rīḥ al-mursalah, the wind sent forth unchecked. The comparison is Ibn ʿAbbas's description of the Prophet's generosity in Ramadan. Mursal here is the ordinary participle and has nothing to do with the hadith grading mursal fixed in the glossary.
'The tribulation' renders al-fitnah, the civil strife among the Muslims in the first generation. It is left as a definite reference because the Sheikh leaves it so.
The Sheikh identifies the subject of the hadith as the Kharijites; that identification is his and is preserved as his.
